title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in Previously Treated HER2-Low Advanced Breast Cancer (DESTINY-Breast04)
abstract: In this randomized phase 3 trial (DESTINY-Breast04), patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer who had received one or two prior lines of chemotherapy were assigned to receive trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) or physician's choice of chemotherapy. Among all patients, median progression-free survival (PFS) was 9.9 months in the trastuzumab deruxtecan group versus 5.1 months in the chemotherapy group (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.50; P<0.001). Overall survival was 23.4 months with T-DXd compared to 16.8 months with chemotherapy (HR 0.64; P=0.001). Interstitial lung disease (ILD) or pneumonitis occurred in 12.1% of patients receiving trastuzumab deruxtecan, predominantly grade 1 or 2, with 0.8% grade 5 events. T-DXd demonstrated significant superiority over standard chemotherapy in HER2-low disease.
content: DESTINY-Breast04 established a new standard of care for HER2-low metastatic breast cancer (defined as IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH negative). Trastuzumab deruxtecan is an antibody-drug conjugate comprising an anti-HER2 humanized monoclonal antibody linked to a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload via a tetrapeptide-based cleavable linker. The high drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR ~8) and membrane-permeable payload induce a potent bystander killing effect on neighboring tumor cells with heterogeneous or low HER2 expression. Adverse event monitoring requires strict vigilance for drug-related interstitial lung disease (ILD), including routine high-resolution CT surveillance and immediate treatment interruption with systemic corticosteroids upon detection.

title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes (SELECT Trial)
abstract: The SELECT multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated subcutaneous semaglutide (2.4 mg once weekly) versus placebo in 17,604 patients aged 45 years or older with preexisting cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity, but without diabetes. Over a mean follow-up of 39.8 months, a primary major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE: cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke) occurred in 569 of 8,803 patients (6.5%) in the semaglutide group and in 701 of 8,801 patients (8.0%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.72 to 0.90; P<0.001). Adverse events leading to permanent discontinuation of the trial drug occurred in 16.6% in the semaglutide group (predominantly gastrointestinal disorders) versus 8.2% in the placebo group.
content: Semaglutide is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that promotes weight loss through central appetite suppression, delayed gastric emptying, and improved glycemic control. The SELECT trial was the first dedicated cardiovascular outcome trial to prove that a pharmacological weight-loss agent can reduce major cardiovascular events in patients without diabetes. Mechanisms of cardiovascular risk reduction are hypothesized to extend beyond body weight reduction, encompassing anti-inflammatory vascular effects, reduced blood pressure, and decreased visceral adiposity.

title: Adagrasib in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Harboring KRAS G12C Mutation (KRYSTAL-1)
abstract: In the phase 2 cohort of the KRYSTAL-1 trial, patients with advanced NSCLC harboring the KRAS G12C mutation who had previously received platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-PD-(L)1 therapy received adagrasib 600 mg orally twice daily. Among 112 evaluable patients, an objective response (confirmed partial or complete response) occurred in 42.9% (95% CI, 33.5 to 52.6). The median duration of response was 8.5 months, and median progression-free survival was 6.5 months. Among patients with co-occurring STK11 mutations, objective response rate was 40.5%. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 44.8% of patients, including elevated alanine/aspartate aminotransferase, fatigue, and nausea. Intracranial objective response in patients with untreated baseline brain metastases was 33.3%.
content: KRAS G12C mutations occur in approximately 13% of non-small cell lung adenocarcinomas. Adagrasib is an irreversible, selective small-molecule inhibitor of KRAS G12C that locks the mutant GTPase in its inactive GDP-bound conformation. Its pharmacokinetic profile features a long half-life (~23 hours), dose-dependent accumulation, and demonstrated central nervous system (CNS) penetration. Co-mutational profiling (STK11/LKB1 and KEAP1) serves as an essential biomarker context, as STK11 co-mutations traditionally confer primary resistance to immune checkpoint blockade but retain clinical sensitivity to targeted KRAS G12C inhibition.

title: Idecabtagene Vicleucel (Ide-cel) CAR T-Cell Therapy in Relapsed Multiple Myeloma (KarMMa)
abstract: The KarMMa phase 2 trial evaluated idecabtagene vicleucel (ide-cel), a B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, in 128 heavily pretreated patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma who had received at least three prior lines of therapy (including an immunomodulatory agent, a proteasome inhibitor, and an anti-CD38 antibody). An overall response was observed in 73% of patients, with complete response or stringent complete response achieved in 33%. Median progression-free survival was 8.8 months across all dose cohorts and 12.1 months in patients receiving the target dose of 450 x 10^6 CAR-positive T cells. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) occurred in 84% of patients (5% grade 3 or higher); neurotoxicity occurred in 18% (3% grade 3).
content: BCMA is selectively expressed on the surface of malignant plasma cells in multiple myeloma, making it an ideal therapeutic target for cellular therapy. Ide-cel incorporates an anti-BCMA single-chain variable fragment (scFv), a 4-1BB costimulatory domain, and a CD3-zeta signaling domain. Management of toxicities is critical: CRS onset typically occurs within 1-2 days post-infusion and requires prompt intervention with tocilizumab (IL-6 receptor antagonist) and dexamethasone. ICANS (Immune effector Cell-Associated Neurotoxicity Syndrome) necessitates neurological surveillance and high-dose corticosteroid protocols.

title: Epcoritamab Monotherapy in Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (EPCORE NHL-1)
abstract: EPCORE NHL-1 was an open-label, multicenter trial evaluating subcutaneous epcoritamab, a bispecific antibody targeting CD3 and CD20, in 157 patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL). At a median follow-up of 10.7 months, overall response rate was 63.1% and complete response rate was 38.9%. Median duration of response was 12.0 months overall, and not reached among patients achieving complete response. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 49.7% of patients (grade 1/2 in 47.1%; grade 3 in 2.5%; no grade 4/5). Subcutaneous step-up dosing and prophylactic corticosteroids mitigated the incidence of severe CRS. Epcoritamab demonstrated durable single-agent activity in a population refractory to prior chemoimmunotherapy and CAR-T therapy.
content: Epcoritamab is an engineered, IgG1-bispecific full-length antibody that simultaneously binds CD3 on endogenous T cells and CD20 on malignant B cells, directing cytotoxic T-cell synapses and perforin/granzyme-mediated apoptosis of lymphoma cells. Subcutaneous delivery provides a slower absorption rate and lower peak plasma cytokine concentrations compared to intravenous bispecifics, significantly reducing the severity of cytokine release syndrome (CRS). This pharmacodynamic property permits outpatient administration after initial step-up monitoring.

title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity (SURMOUNT-1)
abstract: In the phase 3 double-blind SURMOUNT-1 trial, 2,539 adults with an average BMI of 38.0 and at least one weight-related complication (excluding diabetes) were randomly assigned to receive once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide (5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg) or placebo for 72 weeks. The mean percentage change in weight at week 72 was -15.0% with 5 mg, -19.5% with 10 mg, -20.9% with 15 mg, and -3.1% with placebo (P<0.001 for all dose comparisons with placebo). The percentage of participants who achieved a weight reduction of 20% or more was 50% in the 10-mg group and 57% in the 15-mg group, compared to 3% in the placebo group. The most common adverse events were transient, mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal events (nausea, diarrhea, constipation).
content: Tirzepatide is a novel 39-amino-acid synthetic peptide engineered as a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist. Synergistic activation of both incretin receptor pathways produces enhanced metabolic benefits: GIP receptor agonism acts on white adipose tissue to improve insulin sensitivity and lipid storage, and acts in the hypothalamus to synergize with GLP-1 in reducing caloric intake and suppressing nausea. SURMOUNT-1 demonstrated that dual incretin agonism achieves weight loss approaching levels previously attainable only through bariatric surgery.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing with Exagamglogene Autotemcel for Transfusion-Dependent Beta-Thalassemia
abstract: In this single-arm open-label trial (CLIMB THAL-111), patients aged 12 to 35 years with transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia received autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells edited with CRISPR-Cas9 at the erythroid-specific enhancer region of the BCL11A gene (exagamglogene autotemcel [exa-cel]) following myeloablative busulfan conditioning. Of 52 treated patients with adequate follow-up, 48 (92.3%) achieved transfusion independence for at least 12 consecutive months, with weighted average total hemoglobin levels maintained above 11.0 g/dL and high proportions of fetal hemoglobin (HbF > 90%). The safety profile was consistent with busulfan myeloablative conditioning; no malignant clones or off-target gene editing events were observed.
content: Exagamglogene autotemcel (exa-cel / Casgevy) is the first approved therapeutic application of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing. Rather than attempting direct repair of the mutant beta-globin gene (HBB), exa-cel introduces targeted double-strand breaks in the erythroid-specific GATA1-binding motif within the BCL11A enhancer. Downregulation of BCL11A selectively relieves transcriptional repression of the gamma-globin genes (HBG1 and HBG2), reactivating production of fetal hemoglobin (HbF, alpha2-gamma2). High levels of HbF overcome the alpha/beta globin imbalance in beta-thalassemia and eliminate hemolytic anemia.

title: Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy in Advanced Esophageal Cancer (KEYNOTE-590)
abstract: The randomized, double-blind phase 3 KEYNOTE-590 trial investigated first-line pembrolizumab (200 mg every 3 weeks) plus 5-fluorouracil and cisplatin versus placebo plus chemotherapy in 749 patients with previously untreated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic esophageal carcinoma or Siewert type 1 gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. In patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) combined positive score (CPS) >= 10, median overall survival was 13.9 months with pembrolizumab-chemotherapy versus 8.8 months with chemotherapy alone (hazard ratio 0.57; 95% CI 0.43-0.75; P<0.0001). Progression-free survival was also significantly prolonged (median 7.5 vs 5.5 months; HR 0.51). Grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 72% of the pembrolizumab group and 68% of the control group.
content: KEYNOTE-590 established chemoimmunotherapy as the global first-line benchmark for advanced esophageal cancer. Biomarker stratification using the PD-L1 Combined Positive Score (CPS) is clinically imperative: the magnitude of survival benefit correlates strongly with PD-L1 expression levels (CPS >= 10 vs CPS < 10). Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1 binding to PD-L1 and PD-L2, reversing T-cell exhaustion in the tumor microenvironment, while cytotoxic chemotherapy induces immunogenic cell death and antigen release, creating synergistic antitumor immune responses.
